interactionPlan.concept: The visual significance of Fourier Phase versus Amplitude depends on whether an image is characterized by localized structures (which depend heavily on phase) or periodic textures (which depend heavily on amplitude).
learningObjectives: After engaging with this figure, the student will understand that Phase preserves spatial localization and structural edges, while Amplitude captures spatial frequency distribution and periodic directions.
The student will be able to explain why highly textured images are reconstructed recognizable with only original amplitude, whereas sharp, localized objects require original phase.
interactionPlan.keyInsight: Phase preserves the 'where' (spatial structure and boundaries) of localized objects, while amplitude captures the 'what' (dominant frequencies and patterns) of repetitive textures.

interactions.label: Image Type
interactions.effect: Cycles through four source images representing a spectrum from highly localized (bird, horizon) to highly textured (forest, fabric).
interactions.teaches: Demonstrates how Fourier component dominance changes across different classes of visual information.

interactions.label: Phase Noise %
interactions.effect: Progressively randomizes the phase values used in the inverse Fourier reconstruction.
interactions.teaches: Shows how critical phase alignment is to preserving recognizable edges and localized shapes.

interactions.label: Generic 1/f Amp
interactions.effect: Replaces the original amplitude spectrum with a standard 1/f decay profile while keeping the phase intact.
interactions.teaches: Shows that even with standard 1/f amplitude, phase retains enough localized spatial detail to recognize shapes, except in highly periodic textures where amplitude is key.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: A split panel displaying the source image, its 2D DFT Amplitude, and its 2D DFT Phase. On the right, a dynamic reconstructed image updates in real-time using inverse DFT based on the chosen Phase Noise and Amplitude Type. The UI should highlight how texture remains visible under randomized phase for periodic patterns, but localized shapes disintegrate.
